text:
alex: Heads-up — seeing a spike of OOMs on the canary cluster after yesterday's kernel routing change. Mostly on 8k context conv workloads, looks like allocator blowups during kv cache warmup. stack traces attached.

maya: repro steps or a log snippet?

alex: pasted a short log and a flame sample: https://gists.example/kt1. Peak mem ~14.8GB, then OOM at alloc.cu:line 412. Perf snapshot uploaded.

perf-bot: [automated] profile uploaded: /ci/profiles/1766667777 — peak_rss=14.8GB, free_fragments~1.9GB, top_alloc_sites=[conv_kernels.cu:120, kv_cache.cpp:312, allocator.cpp:88]

kevin: did we flip any allocator knobs in staging? @alex I recall I bumped one knob yesterday for batching experiments.

alex: yes — I enabled expandable_segments=true and increased max_split_size_mb 32->64 to reduce splitting overhead for large batched kernels. garbage_collection_threshold was lowered to 0.15 to be more aggressive.

sophie: hmm that combo can backfire: larger max_split_size encourages splits that leave behind many small fragments when long-lived KV pages are pinned. Lower GC threshold means we don't coalesce early.

dan: quick experiment: toggled expandable_segments=false on one canary box and ran the 8k conv workload for 2h — failure rate dropped from 18%->2%. No perf regression on p50 latency.

maya: can you paste the exact config you used?

dan: config snippet: `allocator.expandable_segments=false
allocator.max_split_size_mb=32
allocator.garbage_collection_threshold=0.30` — applied via /etc/redwood/alloc.conf and restarted runtime.

kevin: good to know. Also worth preferring buffer reuse for KV pages instead of freeing+split. Maybe a kvcache.reuse_threshold can help.

alex: proposal for immediate rollback on canary: 1) revert max_split_size_mb -> 32, 2) set expandable_segments=false, 3) increase garbage_collection_threshold to 0.3, 4) add kernel-router guard to prefer smaller kernel variant when workspace would trigger a split. Also add allocator tracing around large kernel calls.

sophie: agree. I'll prepare the canary patch. CL: `CL 5421` — will roll out to 3 hosts in 'batching-small' group and run a 6h soak.

perf-bot: deploy submitted: CL 5421 -> canary 'batching-small' (3 hosts). Healthchecks scheduled.

alex: thanks. If soak looks good we'll make the change the new default and add a short postmortem explaining the interaction. We should also add a unit in allocator fuzz harness for sequence: many small allocs interleaved with long-lived KV writes to catch this pattern.

maya: adding evals + fuzz case to the CI queue. I'll also add an observable: per-host free_fragments over time and post-deploy alert if >1GB fragments persist after 10m.

kevin: once we stabilize, follow-up item: re-evaluate kernel selection heuristics to prefer kernels that use less transient workspace for KV-heavy workloads. That avoids hitting allocator edgecases.

sophie: rolling out now. Will report back after 6h soak. :thumbsup:
